verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the main-board USB-C connector and JST connector destinations as concrete PCB interface requirements.
The client identifies the required panel and touch connectors, adding concrete entries to the main-board connector inventory.
The client specifies the PCB connector count, USB-C count, and JST pin-count characteristic.
The client narrows the low-pin-count PCB constraint to non-interboard connectors, correctly replacing the earlier general characteristic.
The client adds a concrete two-pin JST-GH panel-power-button interface, increasing the main-board JST inventory.
The client specifies the two main-to-sensor-board connectors and their concrete connector types, pin counts, and pitches.
The client requires individual JST interfaces instead of a consolidated fan-out connector, directly constraining the PCB connector architecture.

The source concerns connector-placement feasibility on the later integrated board and does not support the asserted panel-power connector details, destination list, removals, or migration of this main-board Requirement.
